notes.text: One pouch of rice makes about 3 rice balls. Heat the pouches one or two at a time.

move.title: Rice shaped by hand
move.body: Onigiri are Japanese rice balls, packed for school and work lunches. You'll shape warm rice around a tuna filling with damp, salted hands, wrap each one in a strip of seaweed, and cut cucumber sticks with a paring knife to go with them.

why.title: Damp hands, no sticking
why.body: Short-grain rice is sticky, which is why it holds a shape. Water on your hands keeps it sticking to itself instead of to you.

why.title: Salt on your hands
why.body: Rubbing a pinch of salt on your damp palms seasons the outside of each rice ball as you shape it. It's how onigiri are salted in Japan.

why.title: Warm rice, not hot
why.body: Hot rice burns your hands, and cold rice won't stick together. Warm rice, like a bath, is just right.

why.title: Press, turn, press
why.body: Firm, even pressing makes a rice ball that holds together. Press, give it a quarter turn, and press again, three or four times. Squeezing hard makes it dense and gummy.

why.title: The bridge grip on a cucumber
why.body: A cucumber is round and rolls. Cut it in half the long way with the bridge grip first, then lay it flat side down so it can't move.

wrong.sign: The rice sticks to your hands
wrong.fix: Dip your hands in the water again. They should be damp, not dripping.
Press a little firmer, and check the rice is still warm. Cold rice doesn't stick.
Use a little less filling, and pinch a bit more rice over the top before you shape it.
Wrap it on just before eating. Damp rice softens it.

quiz.q: Why do you wet your hands?
choices: So the rice sticks to itself, not to you

quiz.q: How warm should the rice be?
quiz.explain: Hot burns, and cold won't stick.

quiz.q: How do you cut a round cucumber safely?
choices: Halve it with the bridge grip, then lay it flat
quiz.explain: A flat side down stops it rolling.

quiz.q: How long can tuna onigiri sit out?
quiz.explain: Then they go in the fridge.

steps.text: Heat the rice pouches in the microwave as the package says.
steps.tip: Open each pouch away from your face. The steam inside is very hot.

steps.text: Empty the rice into the medium bowl and spread it out with the fork to cool.
steps.look: Warm when you touch it, like a bath, not steaming.

steps.text: Open the tuna with the can opener. Press the lid down and tip out the water over the sink.
steps.tip: The lid's edge is sharp. Press it with a fork, not your fingers.

steps.text: Mix the tuna, mayonnaise, and soy sauce in the small bowl with the fork. Put it in the fridge.
steps.look: Flaky tuna, evenly coated, no big lumps.

steps.text: Lay a damp paper towel under the cutting board so it can't slide. Rinse the cucumber and dry it.
steps.tip: Dry food doesn't slip under the knife.

steps.text: Cut the ends off the cucumber. Hold it with the bridge grip and cut it in half the long way.
Lay each half flat side down. Hold it with the claw grip and cut it into sticks about ½ inch wide.
steps.look: Sticks about as wide as your finger.

steps.text: Set the knife down flat at the top of the board, blade facing away from you.
steps.tip: Do this every time you stop cutting.

steps.text: Fold each nori sheet in half, crease it, and tear along the fold. Fold and tear each half again to make 8 strips.
steps.look: 8 strips about as wide as two fingers.

steps.text: Fill a bowl with the cup of water. Put the salt in a little pile on the plate.
Dip your hands in the water, shake them, and rub a pinch of salt over your palms.
Scoop about ½ cup of rice into one palm. Press a dent in the middle and add a spoonful of tuna.
Cover the tuna with a little more rice. Press it into a triangle, turn it, and press again, three or four times.
steps.look: A firm triangle that holds its shape when you set it down.

steps.text: Make the rest the same way, wetting and salting your hands each time.
Wrap a nori strip around the bottom of each rice ball just before eating. Serve with the cucumber sticks.
steps.tip: Eat within 2 hours, or keep them in the fridge.
